title: Prove sufficient spatial hypotheses for the integrated fourth-moment identity
statement: Let X_t=X0+sqrt(2)B_t on unit torus,X0UNIFORM/independentincrements,V0=0 inR^m,dV_i=g_i(t,X_t).dB_t. Assume smooth deterministic periodic DIVERGENCE-FREE rows and finite-time bounded coefficients. Put a_ij=g_i.dot g_j,Acal_ij=integral a_ij(s,X_s)ds. Uniform spatial density is1. Conditional first-moment densitym_i solvesm_i_t=Delta m_i-sqrt(2)divg_i=Delta m_i,zero initial,so m_i0. Second densitym_ij solvesDelta m_ij+a_ij;conditional bracket densityz_ij solves the SAME equation/zero initial. ThusE[VV^T-Acal|X_t]=0. For fixed symmetric C,D,Ito product differentiation andthis conditional identity replaceVV^T bya deterministic-in-(t,X_t)coefficient pairing withAcal. Integrating givesE[(V_T^T C V_T)(V_T^T D V_T)]=E[tr(CAcal_T)tr(DAcal_T)]+2Etr(CAcal_T D Acal_T). This is an INTEGRATED identity,not conditional Gaussianity. Rotated finite-Fourier heat-gradient rows are divergence free and satisfy finite-time hypotheses. Rough/infinite passage needs actual fourth-moment convergence/uniform integrability;fixed initialx andgeneral adapted integrands are outside scope. Counterexample to the broader claim:stopped BrownianV=B_(t wedge tau),tau first exit(-1,1),hasEV_infinity^4=1 butEtau^2=5/3,so3E[V]_infinity^2=5. Exit equationsu_doubleprime=-2,u=1-x^2,v_doubleprime=-4u,v(0)=5/3 pay the example/time limits. It doesNOT refute the structured theorem. Compensating total/conditional covariance remains equal;no extra18c projected-norm reserve or fulloriginalQC follows.
